international.title: Southern and central Australia face summer of heightened bushfire risk and heatwaves
international.summary: Fire chiefs say large swathes of the country are at risk from fires driven by high fuel loads, dry soil and hot weather Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Large parts of southern and central Australia face elevated fire risk this summer, authorities say, while heatwaves and extreme temperatures are likely nationwide. Most of Victoria, eastern Tasmania and large parts of South Australia, Western Australia, New South Wales and the Northern Territory face heightened bushfire risk – driven by high fuel loads, low soil moisture and forecast hot and dry conditions – according to the seasonal outlook from the Australian and New Zealand Council for Fire and Emergency Services (AFAC), released on Friday.
